description.narrative: The proposed Sustainable Solid Waste Management Project will assist the Government of Uzbekistan (government) to develop the nation's solid waste management (SWM) sector by (i) supporting sector reforms; and (ii) improving access to SWM services for small cities and peri-urban and rural citizens.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Environmental monitoring capabilities of MEEPCC improved Indicator: At least 20 staff (of which at least eight are women) from the Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change's laboratories trained in laboratory testing techniques Progress/Status: In progress.
Staff training will be conducted by the supplier of the mobile environmental laboratory. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and SCEEP report Actual value:

Output: SWM collection and interim disposal services in small urban centers and peri-urban and rural areas improved nationwide Indicator: At least 26 “clean city” education campaigns covering all 13 provinces and with 50% female participation conducted Progress/Status: In progress.
The 'Clean-City' education campaign is being developed by CS3 Consultant and is scheduled for implementation by March 2026. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and personnel list of toza hududs Actual value:

Output: SWM subsector regulatory framework enhanced Indicator: Public consultations with at least 50% participants conducted with at least 50% female participation Progress/Status: In progress: Public consultations were conducted in Fergana, Andijan, Kashkadarya, Surkhandarya, and Tashkent regions in 2025. About 52% from 105 participants were women. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report Actual value:

Output: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change capacity strengthened Indicator: At least 6 officers (of which at least 30% officers are women) from the Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change trained in basic SWM utility management, financial management, gender-responsive HR policy, and SWM system O&M Progress/Status: In progress.
See 2f above. Data Source: Association's training curriculum Actual value:

Output: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change capacity strengthened Indicator: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency to include an asset management division and a performance-based operations division on a pilot basis Progress/Status: In progress.
The Agency's Department for Finance, Economy and Accounting is responsible for asset management. The Agency's Department for Coordination of Activities of Sanitary Cleaning Enterprises is responsible for monitoring performance-based operations. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and annual audit reports Actual value:

Output: Environmental monitoring capabilities of MEEPCC improved Indicator: Environmental testing capabilities of Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change's environmental laboratories upgraded to international standard Progress/Status: In progress.
Procurement of the mobile environmental laboratory has been initiated, with delivery currently estimated by August 2026. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and SCEEP report Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: SWM collection and interim disposal services in small urban centers and peri-urban and rural areas improved nationwide Indicator: 300 SWM collection vehicles (12.0 m3 capacity), 6,000 waste disposal bins (1.1 m3 capacity), 13 excavators, 13 flatbed trucks, and 13 mobile service vehicles commissioned Progress/Status: In progress.
A total of 13 excavators, 13 flatbed trailer trucks, and 300 SWC vehicles have already been commissioned. The commissioning of the remaining 6,000 waste disposal bins is scheduled for Q1 2026, contingent upon finalizing an agreement with the supplier on the certification confirming the quality of the first batch of 1,726 waste disposal bins. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and personnel list of toza hududs Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: SWM collection and interim disposal services in small urban centers and peri-urban and rural areas improved nationwide Indicator: 50 waste transfer containers (20 m3 capacity), 10 units transfer trucks, landfill equipment (15 bulldozer, 15-wheel loaders, 15 excavators), 60 units collection trucks (9 m3), and 40 units collection trucks (14 m3) commissioned Progress/Status: In progress.
30 units hook-lift trucks with 100 units mobile compactor containers (G13) to be commissioned by March 2026; 30 units landfill equipment like bulldozers, excavators and wheel loaders (G9) to be commissioned by March 2025; 60 units full electric SWC vehicles to be commissioned by April 2026; 600 units compact electric waste collection vehicles (G11); 40 units municipal equipment for sanitary cleaning (G12); and 2 units mobile environmental laboratories (G5) to be commissioned by November 2026. The contracts for supply of the above-mentioned equipment include a training how to handle with the new equipment.
Trainings for operational staff of MEEPCC, Agency and operators on SWM operations with gender-sensitivity to be arranged by CS1 and CS3 Consultants, which are scheduled for 2026.
In addition, 12 staff of MEEPCC and the Agency participated in study tours arranged by CS1 Consultant in Spain and Turkey. The visited sites: modern SWM operations with gender-sensitivity aspects; waste sorting and treatments facilities, waste-to-energy plants; customers relations and public education on the waste segregation. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and personnel list of toza hududs Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: SWM collection and interim disposal services in small urban centers and peri-urban and rural areas improved nationwide Indicator: Gender-sensitive information toolkit “zero waste” for schools developed in the local language and distributed to schools in all 13 provinces Progress/Status: In progress.
Gender-sensitive information toolkit “zero waste” for schools is being developed by CS3 Consultant and is scheduled for implementation by March 2026.
Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and personnel list of toza hududs Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: SWM collection and interim disposal services in small urban centers and peri-urban and rural areas improved nationwide Indicator: Special youth-targeted mass media campaign conducted with four gender-responsive knowledge products Progress/Status: In progress.
A special youth-targeted mass media campaign is being designed by CS3 Consultant and is scheduled for implementation by March 2026. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and personnel list of toza hududs Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: SWM subsector regulatory framework enhanced Indicator: Law on waste adopted Progress/Status: In progress: The current Law on Waste of Uzbekistan (No. 362-II) was adopted on 5 April 2002. Recommendations for improving the law were submitted by the Consultant in July 2023 for consideration by the government. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: SWM subsector regulatory framework enhanced Indicator: New gender-responsive regulations to enhance SWM operations adopted Progress/Status: In progress: Draft regulations (legislative initiatives) on environmental taxation for selected commodities, the adoption of container-deposit schemes, municipal solid waste (MSW) collection and transportation, improved guidelines for landfill design and management, and minimum requirements for proper landfill design and environmental performance standards were submitted by the Consultant between October 2022 and July 2023; however, these have not yet been adopted by the government. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: SWM subsector regulatory framework enhanced Indicator: Regulations to improve public accountability and transparent tariff setting methodologies, incorporating gender elements, adopted Progress/Status: In progress: Draft proposals for a tariff bundling system and the application of a “green tariff” for energy generation from waste were prepared by the Consultant between October 2022 and July 2023 and are currently under review by the EA/IA. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change capacity strengthened Indicator: All operators improve their KPIs, as verified by the Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency Progress/Status: In progress.
Implementation of the benchmarking system with KPIs will be monitored by the CS3 Consultant. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and annual audit reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change capacity strengthened Indicator: At least 6 officers from the Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change (of which at least 30% officers are women) received training from an accredited institution Progress/Status: In progress.
A training program at an internationally accredited institution (provisionally in South Korea or Japan) is scheduled for Q1 2026. With support from the CS3 Consultant, the Agency is coordinating with training institutions to finalize the scope and timeline of the program. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and annual audit reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change capacity strengthened Indicator: Gender-responsive customer relations system, with at least 50% of female staff in the Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency, established Progress/Status: In progress. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and annual audit reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change capacity strengthened Indicator: Gender-responsive grievance redress mechanism made operational and sex-disaggregated MIS for customer relations and public reporting established Progress/Status: In progress.
The CS3 Consultant is developing a draft gender-responsive grievance redress mechanism and a sex-disaggregated MIS for customer relations and public reporting, taking into account the Agency's current approach and experience. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and annual audit reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change capacity strengthened Indicator: Performance management framework including KPIs and benchmarking system operational Progress/Status: In progress.
The Performance Management Framework for municipal solid waste (MSW), including key performance indicators (KPIs), was submitted by the CS2 Consultant between November 2022 and March 2023. By June 2026, the CS3 Consultant is expected to support the Agency in operationalizing the performance management framework, including the KPIs and benchmarking system. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and annual audit reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change capacity strengthened Indicator: Sector institutional diagnostic assessment completed Progress/Status: In progress.
The Consultant submitted a review and analysis of the regulatory and institutional frameworks for solid waste management (SWM) in Uzbekistan, together with a diagnostic assessment of the institutional organization of SUE “Toza Hudud,” during the period from September 2022 to June 2023. The institutional diagnostic assessment of the Agency is expected to be completed by March 2026. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports, EA project completion report, and annual audit reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency and Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change capacity strengthened Indicator: Twinning arrangement with an international SWM training and certification facility established Progress/Status: In progress.
The CS3 Consultant is assisting the Agency in establishing a twinning arrangement with an international SWM training and certification facility, scheduled for completion by Q2 2026. Data Source: Signed twinning agreement Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y
Reliable and sustainable SWM services improved and expanded in small urban centers, and peri-urban and rural areas nationwide.

At least 6 million unserved or underserved consumers, including at least 50% women, in small urban centers and peri-urban and rural areas nationwide receive regular SWM collection, transfer, and disposal services. Progress/Status: In progress. To be assessed at completion. Data Source: EA project completion report and survey report. Actual value:

Sex-disaggregated consumer satisfaction with the quality of SWM services increased to 80%. Progress/Status: In progress. To be assessed at completion. Data Source: EA project completion report and survey report. Actual value:

Waste Management and Circular Economy Development Agency's service delivery capacity, including the collection of municipal solid waste in 13 regions, increased to 7,500 tons per day Progress/Status: In progress. To be assessed at completion. Data Source: EA project completion report and survey report. Baseline value: 5000 tons per day
